policy_title: Boost Defence Spending to 2.5% of GDP
stated: The Conservative Party commits to boosting defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, supported by a fully funded plan, to protect British interests and strengthen the UK's position in NATO.

source.quote: Boost defence spending to our new NATO standard of 2.5% of GDP by 2030, so we can protect British interests at home and abroad in an increasingly hostile world.

bearing_set.reason: A sustained increase in defence spending directly affects national security capacity, resilience to external threats, and the UK's NATO posture — all core O5 indicators.

A commitment of roughly £15–20bn/year additional spending (0.5% of ~£2.7tn GDP) materially affects the debt-path and funded-vs-borrowed balance; the 'fully funded' claim is a stated assertion whose credibility is contestable, and if unverified it would widen the structural deficit — a concrete mechanism on a named O12 indicator.

membership_note: O5 is the primary and designed-for bearing; O12 is the mandatory tradeoff check — the scale of the fiscal commitment is large enough that the funding mechanism produces a real verdict regardless of the stated 'fully funded' label. No bearing on O11 (no tax-rate change specified), O3/O7/O8 (no identified cuts to those services in the policy text), or O13 (defence-industrial spillovers are too diffuse and contested to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage).
